title: Sharp stars of a Seville tile panel
subtitle: Tile panel from Seville, V&A, London

construction.note: The finished design was read from Brian Wichmann’s RAY10 drawing, its corners snapped to exact values. We devised the construction. Every star is the same: eight lines touching a small circle about its centre. The star at O comes first; the circles about A copy its lines to the stars at A and at the corners, and one more circle about O gives the lines that close the hexagons round O. The drawing gives no steps.
construction.changes: Wichmann draws the design turned by 45°; it is turned back here so that the tile is the square cell. The compass steps, their order and the named points are ours. The comparison with the drawing checks the finished lines, not how the design was first laid out. The V&A photo of the panel was not checked.

credits.source: Tiling Search, data183/RAY10: Seville tile, V & A
credits.creator: Brian Wichmann
credits.note: The design was read from his drawing. He takes it from the tin-glazed tile panel from Seville in the Victoria and Albert Museum (1005:73 to 84-1884), shown in Anthony Ray, Spanish Pottery 1248–1898 (V&A, 2000), plate 73, and lists a drawing of the El Badi palace, Marrakesh, in Robert Field, Geometric Patterns from Islamic Art and Architecture (Tarquin, 1998), page 26. The construction is ours.

given.O: The centre of a star ringed by hexagons.
given.A: The centre of the next star on the horizontal line.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A.

Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D. Draw a vertical line through each of A and B. Draw a horizontal line through each of C and D. These lines make the square cell, with corners K1, K2, K3 and K4. Draw a straight line through O and K1.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D. Draw a vertical line through A. Draw a horizontal line through C. They cross at K1, a corner of the cell. Draw a straight line through O and K1.

steps.text: The circle crosses the line from O to K1 at E. Draw a vertical line through E. Draw a straight line through A and K2. It crosses the vertical line through E at P. Draw a horizontal line through P. Turn it round O by 90°, three times.

One of the new lines crosses the horizontal line through O at Q. Draw a circle with centre O through Q. It crosses the line from O to K1 at R. Draw a line through R at 90° to the line from O to K1. Turn it round O by 90°, three times. The eight lines make the star at O.

The line through R crosses the horizontal line through O at G. Draw a circle with centre A and radius OG. It crosses the horizontal line through O at S1 and S2. Draw a circle with centre A and the same radius as the circle through Q. It crosses the horizontal line through O at T, left of A.
Draw a line through each of S1 and S2 at 90° to the line from O to K1. Draw a vertical line through T. Turn the three lines round O by 90°, three times. They make the stars at A and at the corners.
Draw a circle with centre O through S1. It crosses the line from O to K1 at V. Draw a vertical line through V. Turn it round O by 90°, three times.
Join K1, K2, K3 and K4 to mark the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Ink the stars at O, at A and at the corners. Ink the hexagons round O and the lines that carry the stars’ sides on.

pattern.text: Put copies of the square cell side by side. A star ringed by eight hexagons sits at every centre, and the stars between them have four.
